title: Quotient of a submodule of a finite-dimensional fraction-field space has bounded length
statement: Let $R$ be a Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] local integral domain of Krull dimension one [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring], let $K$ be its fraction field, let $r$ be a nonnegative integer, and let $M\subseteq K^{\oplus r}$ be any $R$-submodule, without a finite-generation assumption. For every nonzero $x\in R$, the $R$-module $R/xR$ has finite length [def-weil-pbc-module-length], and $M/xM$ has finite length with $\mathrm{length}_R(M/xM)\le r\,\mathrm{length}_R(R/xR)$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00PE (lemma-finite-length, lines 29171-29235), statement and proof

proof.text: Since x≠0 in the domain R, x is a nonzerodivisor. Turn ringKrullDim R=1 into Ring.KrullDimLE 1 R and apply [lem-weil-pbc-dim-le-one-principal-quotient-finite-length]. Identify QuotSMulTop x R with R/(x) to obtain length(R/xR)<∞.

For any strict finite chain p in M/xM, choose a lift m_i∈M of an element in p(i+1) outside p(i). Let N be the finite span of these lifts inside M. Pull the chain back along N/xN→M/xM. Each chosen lift witnesses strictness, so the pulled-back chain q has exactly p.length steps. Map N into the ambient K^r along the subtype of M; it is finitely generated and isomorphic to N. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-dim-one-fg-submodule-quotient-length-bound] and QuotSMulTop.congr to bound length(N/xN), hence p.length, by r length(R/xR). The generic private helper length_quotSMulTop_le_of_fg takes the supremum of all chain lengths via Order.krullDim_eq_iSup_length and Module.coe_length.
The product r length(R/xR) is finite in ENat. The chain bound therefore gives both length(M/xM)<∞ and the desired inequality. This completes the unchanged conjunction.

split_report.summary: Split following the proof of Stacks 00PE exactly (checked 00PE, 00IV, 00KH in algebra.tex and the tags file). Nine steps: R/xR of finite length (new Mathlib leaf lem-weil-pbc-dim-le-one-principal-quotient-finite-length = isFiniteLength_quotient_span_singleton); the unit case; reduction to M spanning a K^{r'} with r' <= r; the finite case by clearing denominators, an integer c with x^c R^{r'} ⊂ M (Stacks' 'R^{⊕r}/M has finite length, in particular ...' written out via d R^{r'} ⊂ M and x ∈ sqrt(dR), citing lem-weil-pbc-zero-locus-eq-iff-radical-eq), length(N/x^nN) = n length(N/xN), length(F/xF) = r' length(R/xR), and the sandwich, all through the new Mathlib leaf lem-weil-pbc-length-additive-short-exact (00IV, Module.length_eq_add_of_exact); the general case by the chain argument of the last paragraph. Not 'induction on r' as the lead's prompt suggested: the Stacks proof uses the sandwich, and the split follows it. Statement unchanged.
